feedback: No race has been run yet, so this feedback rests only on the contract and on the choices I had to make to build the controller for this geometry. The five-sensor array at 10 mm spacing and 12 mm footprint gives every sensor a non-zero reading when the 25 mm tape is under the array, so the signal is continuous. That means the controller does not need a large kd to keep the signal smooth (I used kd 0.05). The sensors sit 50 mm ahead of the axle, and with weights of ±2 at the outer sensors the signal saturates at about ±2 units. I used kp 2.5 to keep full correction within the PWM range. The Builder should interpret the next race this way. If line_loss_events is above zero on the slalom or s-bend while max_error stays small, the array is not covering the tape at sharp bends, so widen the span (for example x = ±0.02 m is the current edge; try ±0.03 m) before changing the wheels. If steering_oscillation is high with max_error low, the robot is over-reacting: reduce sensor span or mass, or move the sensors closer to the axle so the controller reacts to a shorter lead. If completion_time is above 3.0 s with no line loss, the robot is speed-limited: reduce mass or increase wheel_radius, since top speed does not come from the controller (base_speed is already 1.6 of 2). The Integrator will report which of these conditions held.
requested_changes: If the next race shows line_loss_events > 0 with max_error near the 0.06 m limit on the slalom or s-bend, widen the sensor array to x = ±0.03 m (weights stay proportional to x) and keep sensor_size 0.012.
If the next race shows completion_time > 3.0 s with no line loss, reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg or increase wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m to raise speed.

If the next race shows steering_oscillation high while max_error is low, move the sensors to y = 0.04 m (less lead) and keep the same x positions, to test whether the 50 mm forward offset is too far ahead.
